title: Practice adoption can outrun hard evidence; de-adoption needs a correction surface separate from the negative result itself
summary: Candidate pattern opened in rev0013: plausible and widely adopted medical practices can persist until hard-endpoint, sham-controlled, pooled, or systematic evidence narrows/reverses them; however, publication of negative evidence is not the same as de-adoption. The pattern adds a correction-surface vocabulary for guidelines, systematic reviews, grading, coverage, low-value-care lists, and patient/clinician conversations.

claims.claim: Across high-dose chemotherapy for breast cancer, knee arthroscopy for osteoarthritis, vertebroplasty, and renal-artery stenting, plausible or adopted practices were later narrowed or reversed by randomized, sham-controlled, hard-endpoint, or pooled evidence.

claims.claim: Medical reversal is not finished when a negative trial is published; de-adoption requires correction surfaces such as systematic reviews, recommendation grading, guidelines, coverage rules, low-value-care lists, and patient-clinician conversation tools.

type_payload.candidate_status_reason: four medical negative-result/reversal cases plus one meta-research audit and five infrastructure records support a shared question, but adoption curves and guideline histories are incomplete
recurring_mechanisms_to_test: uncontrolled improvement mistaken for procedure-specific benefit
surrogate/procedural success mistaken for patient benefit

positive_controls_needed: Add more cases where adoption outran hard evidence and de-adoption required a separate correction surface.
negative_controls_needed: Add practices that de-adopted quickly after negative evidence, and negative results that did not warrant de-adoption because subgroup indications remained.
counterexamples_to_seek: A practice-lag narrative where utilization changed for reimbursement or supply reasons rather than evidentiary correction.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: High: adoption, coverage, guideline, utilization, patient preference, and subgroup exception surfaces need separate child records.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Clinical reversals can involve real patients who made choices under uncertainty; avoid hindsight contempt.
Do not treat procedure de-adoption as a patient-specific treatment recommendation.
Preserve the difference between “no benefit in studied population” and “never useful.”

revision_history.change: Claim support migrated to typed evidence_refs; factual claim text and statuses unchanged.
Added red_team_controls with positive/negative controls, counterexample search, rollback triggers, and maturity gate.

unknowns: The pattern is supported by a cluster of reversal and infrastructure records, but does not yet include negative controls where adoption appropriately followed strong evidence.
Practice-lag duration, utilization curves, coverage history, and guideline chronology are not yet consistently encoded for child cases.
The pattern could split into at least three subpatterns: premature adoption, slow de-adoption, and correction-surface insufficiency.
next_actions: Add controls and counterexamples before any maturity promotion.
Create child status-transition records for guideline, payer, and practice-use milestones in each supported medical-reversal case.
Define rollback triggers: evidence of appropriate early adoption, rapid de-adoption, or substantial subgroup benefit should narrow the pattern.
Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
